title: 1 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 2
description: Ten questions on 1 Corinthians 2: preaching in weakness rather than persuasive words, God's wisdom in a mystery, and the Spirit who searches all things.

questions.text: How does the writer say he did not come to them?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:1 says that when he came to them he did not come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to them the testimony of God.

answers.text: With letters of recommendation
With excellence of speech or of wisdom
With gifts for the poor
With companions from Jerusalem

questions.text: What did he determine to know among them?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:2 says he determined not to know anything among them except Jesus Christ and him crucified.

answers.text: Jesus Christ and him crucified
The law and the prophets
The wisdom of the Greeks
The mysteries of the rulers

questions.text: In what condition does he say he was with them?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:3 says he was with them in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.

answers.text: In boldness, in joy, and in much rejoicing
In honor among the rulers of this world
In sickness of body and nothing more
In weakness, in fear, and in much trembling

questions.text: In what were his speech and his preaching, instead of persuasive words of human wisdom?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 says his speech and preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power.

answers.text: In the letter of the law and its ordinances
In parables and riddles of the wise
In demonstration of the Spirit and of power
In the traditions received from the fathers

questions.text: In what was their faith to stand?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:5 says this was so that their faith would not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

answers.text: In the wisdom of men
In the power of God
In the witness of the apostles
In their own works

questions.text: What would the rulers of this world not have done, had they known God's wisdom?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:7-8 say that God's wisdom in a mystery was known by none of the rulers of this world, for had they known it they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

answers.text: They would not have crucified the Lord of glory
They would not have divided the kingdom
They would not have persecuted the apostles
They would not have destroyed the temple

questions.text: For whom has God prepared the things an eye did not see and an ear did not hear?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:9 quotes that things which an eye did not see and an ear did not hear, which did not enter into the heart of man, God has prepared for those who love him.

answers.text: For the wise of this world
For the rulers of this world
For those who seek signs
For those who love him

questions.text: Who alone knows the things of God, according to the text?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:11 says that as only the spirit of a man knows the things of a man, so no one knows the things of God except God's Spirit.

answers.text: The prophets
The full grown
God's Spirit
The spirit of the world

questions.text: Why doesn't the natural man receive the things of God's Spirit?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:14 says the natural man does not receive them, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot know them because they are spiritually discerned.

answers.text: Because no one has ever told him about them
Because they are foolishness to him and spiritually discerned
Because they are written in a mystery and sealed
Because the rulers of this world forbid it

questions.text: What does the writer say “we” have, in the last verse of the chapter?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:16 asks who has known the mind of the Lord to instruct him, and says, “But we have Christ's mind.”

answers.text: Christ's mind
The mind of the full grown
The spirit of the world
The wisdom of the rulers
